content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm pleased to join this technical [company_name] community. I've worked on some basic projects with the [product_name] using [product_name] V6, and now I'm developing a solution that needs to cut plastic extruded strips to a specific length. The process will be: 1. The desired length is input into the system (in inches or centimeters, with two or three decimal places; lengths range from 12" to 144"). 2. The length is measured in real time using an incremental encoder with 600 CPR and a 3-inch wheel. 3. Once the target length is reached, the PLC activates a cutter or saw, restarting the cycle. This seems to be a common setup, so any programming advice or wiring tips for connecting the encoder to the [product_name] for handling up/down counting, and advice on how many inputs are required for the encoder, would be appreciated.

Hello [user_name], welcome to the forum. Could you specify the pulse interval for your encoder? In my view, for time-critical A/B signal processing of encoders, the [product_name] isn't an ideal fit. I recommend considering the [product_name] [version_no] instead.

Hello [user_name], thank you very much for your quick response. My application doesn't involve high-speed operation—the line moves at 1–10 meters per minute (about 2–20 cm/sec). Using an encoder with 600 CPR and a measuring wheel with a diameter of approximately 7.5 cm, we're looking at roughly 42 to 420 pulses per second. Regards, [user_name]

Hello [user_name], you won't be able to achieve this with the [product_name]. The standard inputs are limited to a frequency of 4 Hz, which makes them and the program too slow for your requirements. The 'fast' inputs allow up to 5 kHz, but they can't be used for your scenario. Unfortunately, the [product_name] lacks the necessary features to accurately process incremental encoder signals at higher speeds. Regards, [user_name]

Thank you, [user_name]. I’ll look into the [product_name] [version_no] as recommended, even though I'm not familiar with this system yet. I’ll try it since the project is important, and I’ll certainly need further assistance with future [product_name] projects.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discussed applying the [product_name] in a measure-and-cut scenario using an incremental encoder, but identified that its input frequency limits make it inadequate for properly processing encoder pulses. Both standard and fast inputs on the module cannot handle the signal requirements for this application, leading users to suggest considering a different [company_name] product for reliable operation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user anticipated the [product_name] would reliably interface with an incremental encoder, processing several hundred pulses per second and accurately controlling a cutter for precise measurements.
